_comment: DESIGN §4.6. The system is ✅; the contents were ❓ (§15.11). This is a 🟡 first pass written as a data-file default in an unattended session (CLAUDE.md, Ways of working) and listed in docs/CAPSULE-SESSION-2026-09-20.md for confirmation. Three ranks, each gated on a Library tier. Nothing here is ever lost: research survives collapse and Rome's intervention (Pillar 7).

nodes.name: The surveyor's groma
nodes.description: Right angles struck from a plumbed cross. Foundations stop being argued over.

nodes.name: Two-field rotation
nodes.description: Half the land rests while half is sown. The ground gives more for it.

nodes.name: Charcoal burning
nodes.description: Wood smothered under turf burns hotter and travels lighter.

nodes.name: Opus caementicium
nodes.description: Lime, rubble and volcanic ash. It sets in the wet and it does not care about the frost.

nodes.name: Raised granaries
nodes.description: Floors lifted on stone piers, air beneath, vermin locked out.

nodes.name: The tapped bloomery
nodes.description: Slag drawn off while the furnace still runs, so the fire is never let go cold.

nodes.name: The double ledger
nodes.description: Two books kept of every sum, and a clerk who compares them. Less sticks to the fingers.

nodes.name: Torsion engines
nodes.description: Sinew ropes wound until they scream, and a bolt that goes through a shield wall.

nodes.name: The colonial census
nodes.description: Every head counted, every trade written down. A colony that knows itself can hold more of itself.

nodes.name: Via munita
nodes.description: A metalled road with a crown and ditches. Carts come through in the wet, and so do envoys.

nodes.name: The archives
nodes.description: Deeds, judgements and genealogies kept where the council must consult them — and your house keeps the keys.
